messages:
maria: quick heads-up — I opened a draft PR that surfaces an SLO-level notification template in the console. aim is: let tenants set a default notify payload per SLO (channels, severity, quiet windows) instead of only per-route. PTAL for API shape + rollout UX.
kevin: nice. can you paste the API shape here? trying to reason about migration from per-route defaults.
maria: sure, current proposal (draft):
```json
POST /api/v1/tenants/:t/slo/:s/notify-template
{
  "channels": ["pagerduty:team-x", "email:eng@acme.com"],
  "severity": "critical",
  "quiet_windows": [ { "dow": "sat", "start": "00:00", "end": "06:00" } ],
  "sampling": { "mode": "adaptive", "target_qps": 0.5 },
  "notify_budget": { "monthly_units": 1000 }
}
```
idea is console shows a per-SLO preview of "expected fanout" (estimate) and a small link to "apply to routes" to copy template to matching routes.
ash: i like the preview. how do we compute expected fanout? telemetry team will need to expose per-tenant subscription counts, right?
maria: yes — backend endpoint will call /telemetry/estimate_fanout?ten=... using last-30d active subscriptions + channel heuristics (PD integrations count as 1, email as 1, slack webhooks multiply by configured hooks). estimate = sum(channel_multiplier * active_subscriptions) * sample_rate
kevin: two concerns: 1) per-route overrides must still be allowed (we only copy as a baseline). 2) quotas: if templates let tenants set big fanouts, we should show quota impact and warn about notify_budget and noise.
jordan: +1. also need an API-level flag for "enforce_quota" vs "warn only" for enterprise customers.
ops-bot: notify-quota-checker ran on draft payload: projected monthly units=4200 which exceeds tenant commit 2000. :warning:
maria: yeah plan is to show a red badge in the preview and a tooltip: "Projected notify units exceed tenant reserved budget" and a one-click "request burst" that opens ticket to sales/ops.
sam: UX nit: the console should let users preview per-route after applying template, but default to showing a representative sample of 5 routes (not thousands). expand on demand.
kevin: for the internal API debate: do we add a new field on the SLO resource (slo.notify_template) or a separate resource (slo_notify_templates)?
ash: separate resource gives better lifecycle: templates can have version, rollout history, who applied. storing on slo means it's always inlined and harder to diff.
jordan: separate resource + reference on SLO is my vote. then console can show versions and a "rollback" button.
maria: agreed — draft PR does sep resource. also proposing a server-side canary rollout: new field notify_template_reference with rollout_policy { type: canary, percent: 10 } so we only apply the template to first 10% of routes during rollout.
kevin: how do we define 10% of routes deterministically? random by route id hash with tenant salt? need to keep it stable across re-deploys.
ash: use stable hashing on route_id with tenant salt + rollout epoch. that way when percent increases, we add more. add a toggle to recompute sample to preview.
sam: telemetry question: when a template is applied we should emit an event slo.template.apply with fields: template_id, routes_affected_count, projected_units, actual_fanout_sample (top 5), applied_by. can we get that in the proposal?
maria: yes will add the event. also thinking of adding a periodic "template health" job that compares projected vs actual and flags >30% mismatch for quality regression alerts.
kevin: backcompat: when migrating existing per-route defaults, do we create a template per-tenant automatically and mark routes as referencing it? risk: might spike notifications if template has slightly different channels.
jordan: migration should be conservative: auto-create template but do not apply it to routes. console shows a migration assistant with checklist and dry-run apply.
maria: exactly. PR includes migration job that just generates candidates and populates console suggestions; ops will run it and owners approve.
ash: small code-level ask: please include in API the sample_rate and sample_window so backend can do consistent estimations. don't bake sampling logic into console JS.
maria: ack — will move sampling calc to backend and expose an estimate endpoint that returns { projected_units, sample_examples: [route_id...], mismatch_reasons: [...] }
kevin: lgtm overall. one more: add an "auditing" policy so changing templates requires at least two approvers for tenants with >X reserved units.
sam: +1, compliance asked for that on prod tenants.
maria: thanks all — i'll update the draft with these notes. leaving the PR link here: https://git.internal/repo/pulls/1872 (draft). will ping again when updated. :zap:
ops-bot: pull request 1872 changed files: console/slo_notify_ui, api/slo_notify_templates, telemetry/estimator — CI queued. :white_check_mark:
